issue: `status()` is now a mutating read path: every refresh (mount, `r`, stage, unstage, rm, ignore, push, pull, encrypt, commit) shells out to gpg via `secret hide -m`, and `commit()` hides a second time immediately after the refresh that just hid — no dedup or throttle
reason: Accepted. `git secret hide -m` re-encrypts only files whose plaintext changed, so the repeat is a no-op walk in the common case; deduplicating needs session state tracking the last hide, which costs more than it saves.

issue: Raw git-secret/gpg stderr is interpolated verbatim into the on-screen message (`f"hide failed: {err}"` then `f"Error refreshing status: {exc}"`), so gpg key ids and absolute paths reach the UI unfiltered and untruncated
reason: Accepted. dot's TUI is a single-user local tool on the user's own dotfiles; showing the operator their own gpg key ids and home paths discloses nothing new, and verbatim stderr is what makes a hide failure diagnosable.

reason: Accepted. The entry exists and ships with the PRD; squashing b6a8cb7 into a0f45b7 rewrites already-made history for no user-visible gain.

issue: FileEntry.is_secret is dead in production: GitOps.status() marks it with `filepath in secrets`, but `cfg secret list` emits PLAINTEXT paths (`.ssh/config`) while `git status --porcelain` emits the tracked CIPHERTEXT path (`.ssh/config.secret`), because git-secret gitignores the plaintext. The two never match, so the TUI's file list never renders its secret marker (src/tools/dot/tui/widgets/file_list.py:92).
reason: Pre-existing and out of PRD 00046's scope; the fix needs a UX decision about what the TUI shows for a hidden secret. Recorded in the batch deferred JSON for batch end.
